faq: Do users need to reinstall the app?
No. The new design ships as a normal update from Google Play. Accounts, saved data and settings stay as they are, and we test the update from your current version before handover.
Will the redesign work on small phones and tablets?
We design for common phone sizes and check the layout on a small and a large phone. Tablet and foldable layouts are a separate service, though the new components are built to scale.
Do you need the existing source code?
Yes, because we rebuild the screens inside your project. Send a repository invite. If the source is lost, tell us before ordering, as that needs a different plan.
Can I choose Material You dynamic colors?
Yes, if it suits your brand. Material You can adapt colors to the user's wallpaper on Android 12 and later, or we can keep your fixed brand colors. We can show both in the mockups.

Ecom Swift LLC delivers an Android app redesign with Material design: a fresh, consistent interface for your existing app, rebuilt in Jetpack Compose or XML, while your features, accounts and user data stay exactly as they are.

## What is an Android app redesign?

An Android app redesign changes how the app looks and how people move through it, without changing what it does. Colors, type, spacing, icons, navigation and layouts get a fresh, consistent treatment, usually based on Material 3, Google's design system for Android.

Your backend, your users and your saved data are not touched. People update the app through the normal Play Store update and find a cleaner version of the product they already use.

## Why an older interface holds an app back

Screens built over several years often look like a patchwork. Buttons differ from screen to screen, spacing changes, text is hard to read on small phones and dark theme is missing. New users read that as neglect, and existing users find it tiring.

Navigation is often the bigger problem. Features that were added one at a time end up buried in menus, so people cannot find what the app can do. A redesign tidies the structure as well as the surface.

## How a redesign affects usability and retention

A clear interface reduces effort. When the main action is obvious, text is readable and tap targets are large enough, more people finish what they came to do. That can lift satisfaction and reduce support questions. It will not fix a product that lacks a useful purpose, and we cannot promise a particular change in ratings or revenue.

Consistency also saves money later. A small set of reusable parts, such as buttons, cards and list rows, lets future screens be built faster and look right by default.

## What a good Android redesign includes

- A walkthrough of your current flows, to find where users hesitate.
- New designs for approval before any code is changed.
- Material 3 colors, type scale and spacing applied across the redesigned screens.
- Reusable components for buttons, cards, lists and inputs.
- Dark theme support, so the app respects the phone's setting.
- Layouts that work on small phones, large phones and tablets.
- A simpler navigation structure for the main flows.
- A pass over text size and contrast for readability.
- Adaptive icon refresh and polished transitions in the fuller packages.
- Design files and a short style guide at handover.

## How we work

You share the app and, if you want us to build the new interface in your project, the source code. We study your most used screens, propose new designs and wait for your approval. Then we rebuild the interface in Jetpack Compose or in XML, depending on what your project uses, and test the update from your current version to the new one so that sign-in and saved data survive.

The Basic package refreshes a few key screens with new colors, type, spacing and mockups. Standard covers the main flows with a small component kit, onboarding and dark theme. Premium delivers a complete redesign with navigation changes, accessibility checks, motion and design files.

## What helps and what hurts

**Do:**
- Tell us which screens people use most.
- Keep brand colors, but allow us to adjust shades for contrast.
- Approve designs before development begins.
- Plan to release the update to a small group first.
- Keep your feature list unchanged during the redesign.

**Avoid:**
- Redesigning every screen when only a few cause trouble.
- Copying iOS patterns that fight the Android back gesture.
- Using tiny text to fit more on the screen.
- Changing icons so much that long-time users get lost.
- Mixing a redesign with new data structures in the same release.

## Who this is for

An owner whose app works well but looks dated beside newer rivals. A business that has added features for years and ended up with a crowded interface. A founder who needs the app to look credible before a launch push or a funding conversation. A team that wants dark theme and Material 3 without a rewrite.

## What we need from you

Send the app name, a test account, your brand guide if you have one and a few examples of apps you admire. Source code access is helpful and is given as a collaborator invite. If you do not have the code, we can deliver designs your developer can use. We never ask for passwords.
